question.text: Stock exchanges must comply with the SEBI Master Circular by:

answer.text: Implementing all prescribed requirements in their trading rules, clearing procedures, and surveillance mechanisms
Simply acknowledging receipt of the circular
Complying only with provisions they agree with
Implementing changes within 5 years of the circular

explanation.text: The Logic: Compliance with a SEBI Master Circular is mandatory for recognised stock exchanges. In practice, this means stock exchanges have to operationalise all prescribed requirements in their bye-laws, trading rules, clearing procedures, surveillance systems and investor-protection mechanisms, and demonstrate ongoing adherence to SEBI through reporting and inspection. The Trap: Simply acknowledging the circular, cherry-picking provisions, or stretching implementation over many years would all be non-compliance. The circular's directions are binding once issued. Note: The combined compliance obligation across trading rules, clearing procedures, and surveillance mechanisms under the SEBI Master Circular is not laid out in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages — those pages reference only specific circular-driven items such as contract size, dynamic price-band criteria and algo-trading controls. The framing above reflects general SEBI compliance-practice knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
